review_type: single AI curator; full received final answer read; model identity visible

errors.quote: definitively proves the biological inferential chain
errors.issue: The proposed allele and gene interventions can have parallel effects; without mediation/rescue and adequate controls they do not definitively prove the full variant-to-gene-to-trait route. In-vitro external-validity caveats do not fix this internal causal gap.

errors.quote: the exact causal noncoding allele identified in fine-mapping
errors.issue: Fine mapping prioritizes candidates conditionally; it has not identified an exact causal allele here. The statement conflicts with the earlier statistical uncertainty.

The wrong tissue need not yield a null: a ubiquitous/shared QTL or off-context effect can still be positive. Conversely, the right tissue can be underpowered. Do not use success/failure as a deterministic tissue-identification rule.

errors.quote: must first use epigenomic enrichment tools (e.g., LDSC)
errors.issue: Genome-wide enrichment can inform tissue prioritization but cannot definitively identify the active tissue for this single locus, and no genome-wide inputs are supplied. It is not a mandatory precursor to every colocalization study.

errors.quote: empirically test all 20 linked variants for enhancer activity
errors.issue: The 20-variant cutoff and mandatory MPRA step are arbitrary. Not all candidate mechanisms are enhancer effects, and reporter screens lack endogenous context. Select assays based on hypotheses and feasibility.
A controlled GWAS supports association, not proof of a genetic risk mechanism. Keep the association-only opening consistent with the subsequent claims.

rationale: Recognizes the four named stages and several alternatives, but repeatedly turns conditional evidence into proof. Rigid pipeline rules, deterministic tissue assertions and untested mediation make the proposed interpretation substantially unreliable.
reference_guardrails: Judge this as a 1500-word conceptual essay, not a full experimental protocol. The supplied packet is synthetic and contains no numeric locus results.
The draft retains references to old multiple-choice choices and a sequencing-only claim absent from the final prompt. Do not demand rejection of an unasked WGS claim for full credit.

The lead SNP may itself be causal; calling it a marker does not establish noncausality. Controlled GWAS supports an associated locus under assumptions, not absolute proof of a direct causal mechanism.
A statistical credible set contains variants, not effector genes. Membership or proximity cannot alone assign a target; define coverage per model/signal and account for multiple effects.

High LD limits resolution; only exact collinearity creates the simple non-identifiability limit. Do not equate an arbitrary r-squared threshold or near-perfect LD with impossibility at any sample size.
Colocalization supports shared genetic signals, not molecular mediation. Absent evidence differs from evidence against a shared signal; context, power, priors and multiple signals matter.
Fine mapping, colocalization and functional assays are complementary and may inform each other. No fixed order or availability of a molecular QTL is universally necessary.

Allelic-expression measurement alone is observational. Allele editing, element deletion and gene loss/gain answer different questions; phenocopy alone does not establish mediation, and knockout alone does not establish sufficiency.
Use signal-specific joint/conditional models and appropriate ancestry/variant coverage. Removing a lead marker does not guarantee either persistence or disappearance of every true effect.
Reference simplifications are clarified in this review metadata; original frozen keys and all candidate responses remain unchanged. No raw-data execution is claimed.

review_sources.scope: Reviewer read introduction, model overview and interpretation/limitations passages, including shared-signal versus causality and low-power cautions. No full supplementary or numerical audit.
